Commentary.Commentary: We are back for West Indies' second innings. The Sri Lanka players are out in the middle. John Campbell and Kraigg Brathwaite will open the innings for West Indies. Suranga Lakmal will start the proceedings for Sri Lanka.

Right! West Indies take the lead of 96. They have plenty of time to bat in this game. Interesting to see what their approach will be when they come out to bat. Sri Lanka will need early wickets and that will help them keep West Indies batting in check. Join us for the West Indies batting in a short while.

West Indies were really good with the ball on this flat deck. They bowled their hearts out on Day 3 in the limited opportunity that they got after rain interruptions. Roach bagged a 3-fer and wrapped up the things quickly here. Apart from Cornwall, every bowler managed at least a wicket to his name. Holder was superb in his 21-over spell as he gave just 39 runs and picked up 2 wickets. Overall, a great bowling performance from the hosts.

On Day 3, Sri Lanka lost the plot as they lost 5 wickets in quick time after a decent recovery act by Dinesh Chandimal and Dhananjaya de Silva. Towards the end of the rain-curtailed Day 3, Nissanka held onto his end and made sure they were not bundled out on that day itself. He battled hard in the middle for his half ton and took the team's score to over 250. Apart from him, only Thirimanne got to a half-century. The likes of Fernando, de Silva, Chandimal and Dickwella got good starts but they failed to bat long.

Just 23 balls is what the hosts took to bundle the Sri Lankans. And they also take a vital 96 runs lead. Roach is the man who does the job in one over. Nissanka did get to his half ton but he had to play his shots. And he eventually fell and the Sri Lankan innings have been rolled over.

Hello and welcome to Day 4 of the second and final Test between West Indies and Sri Lanka. It was rain, which dominated Day 3 but in the play we got, West Indies bowlers did a fantastic job on a flat pitch. The hosts are just two wickets away from wrapping up the Lankan innings. It was a very tame performance from the visitors on Day 3 and they would be thankful for rain otherwise they might have already been bowling. Pathum Nissanka is still out in the middle and the onus will be on him to reduce the remaining 104 runs deficit that still remains. A very crucial penultimate day of this Test awaits us. Stay tuned for further updates.
... Day 4, Session 1 ...

Right then! Sri Lanka would take the rain as a reliever while West Indies would rue that thing. They would feel that they had the chance to bowl Sri Lanka out but now they will have to come back on Day 4 to complete the formality. Sri Lanka, on the other hand, would want Nissanka to bat along with the remaining batsmen and reduce the deficit to some extent. They would also get the chance to rework on their gameplan for the rest of the match. Remember it is an early start to compensate for the lost overs on Day 3. 98 overs are scheduled for the remaining two days. How many can we get? To know more how will Day 4 turn out, join us on 1st April 2021 at 0930 local (1330 GMT). Till then, take care and cheers!

With the ball for West Indies, all the bowlers bowled well and kept West Indies ahead by picking wickets regularly. Except Rahkeem Cornwall all the bowlers that Kraigg Brathwaite used produced a wicket. Joseph and Holder bagged a couple of them as others had a wicket to their name. Blackwood bowling part-time spin too got a wicket though a lucky wicket but West Indies and Jermanine would take it anyway.

Sri Lanka did not start well with the bat as they lost Chandimal and de Silva both in quick succession after they staged a fightback with a 75-run stand but Chandimal fell prey to the short ball from Gabriel. De Silva soon followed where he could have reviewed and stayed as he was given out LBW but the ball was going down leg. Since then Pathum Nissanka kept on motoring the innings but he lost Dickwella and then Lakmal before rain played riot for most part of the day. When the play resumed in the final session, Dushmantha Chameera was the last one to go as rain again paid a visit to bring an early close to the play. Nissanka though is batting on 49 and he has Embuldeniya out there for support who is yet to get off the mark. Pathum would look to minimalise the damage with the final two wickets when the game begins on Day 4.

That ends the moving day of this 2nd Test between Sri Lanka and West Indies. It was rain which dictated the terms all day and also had the final laugh. All applause for the West Indies pacers who have bowled their heart out to get wickets on this docile surface. Sri Lanka still trail by 104 runs and they just have Pathum Nissanka out there along with two remaining bowlers.
So the inevitible has happened. Yes, the STUMPS are drawn on this rain marred third day.

Pathum Nissanka has looked settled so far in his short stay as Niroshan Dickwella has just joined him out in the middle.

Another happening session in this Test comes to an end and West Indies would be a lot happier side going into Lunch. While Sri Lanka too won't be disappointed as they have scored runs despite losing Dinesh Chandimal early on Day 3.

We are all set to begin Day 3. The West Indies players are out in the middle. Dinesh Chandimal and Dhananjaya De Silva will resume their innings for Sri Lanka. Shannon Gabriel will start the proceedings for West Indies.

Pitch Report - Samuel Badree is down for the pitch report along with Sir Curtly Ambrose. Badree says that there is a 20% chance of rain today. Sir Curtly says that these are batting-friendly conditions. He further says there is nothing for the bowlers barring a few deliveries from Roach. He ends by saying that West Indies need to strike early to gain the advantage.

Kyle Mayers is down for an interview. He says that it was not easy batting on this track. On being asked about taking wickets, Mayers says that he tries to bowl good length deliveries. Mentions that he tries to execute his plans and takes advice from coaches. Further says that they will look to restrict Sri Lanka and not let them take a huge lead.

So far the 2nd Test between Sri Lanka and West Indies have swung like a pendulum. No team has been able to assert itself completely on the other so far. If Sri Lanka were on top for the maximum part of Day 1 then a resurgence from West Indies saw them end Day 1 ahead of their opponents. Day 2 was similar as West Indies began strongly and had the entire first session in their control as well as the second to some extent but then in the third session, a strong stand between Dinesh Chandimal and Dhananjaya de Silva ensured that the West Indies bowlers are kept at bay. So, now welcome to Day 3 of this Test. Also known as the moving day that will decide where this game will head. Sri Lanka still need 218 runs to get into the lead. For that to happen they will need this partnership to bat long and deep. Will that happen? Or will the West Indian bowlers run riot to bundle the Lankans? The action unfolds in a short while.
... Day 3, Session 1 ...

Right then. That brings another fine Day of Test cricket to an end. Both the teams have fought well and there is no clear team, which is ahead in the game and that is what is intriguing about this Test match. They say that Day 3 is the moving Day in the red-ball game and it will be interesting to see which team, moves to the way of a win on Day 3, which will begin at 1000 local (1400 GMT). Do join us for the same. Until then, cheers!

Jason Holder is in for a quick chat! He says that they heard a noise and tells they thought there was an edge but feels the umpire saw day-light between bat and ball. Holder says he will need to go upstairs and check it. Tells it is a very flat and docile wicket, so they needed some energy and it was his duty to motivate them and hence the chirping. Credits the bowlers as he feels that it has been a great effort from them. Holder feels it is very even-steven at the moment. Feels if they can make the second new ball count then it can tilt their way. Holder says that he has been toiling but has not got the wicket today but adds that is the nature of the game.

West Indies would have been happy with their runs on the board, at the end of their batting but with the way the skipper was motoring along, they would have wanted him to try and some more runs to their name. With the ball, they had some success early on in the day, and Roach, Mayers, and Joseph had wickets to their name, while the rest of the bowlers, were yet to grab a wicket. But when Dinesh and de Silva were going about their business, they were not able to ask too many questions and they will look to break this stand early, on Day 3.

Sri Lanka would have wanted to dismiss the West Indian batters early in the first session, but they were only able to do that, just at the stroke of Lunch, as the hosts finished with 354, to their name. They started off tentatively, with the bat, as they lost their skipper early on. Two more wickets were lost early on, in the evening session but since then, the duo of Chandimal and de Silva have done well to add a stand of 59-runs to their name and have seen the day off nicely for the visitors.

Another brilliant day of Test cricket, which, just like the first day and had its fair share of battle between bat and ball, although the battle was not as intense, as it was on Day 1. Both the teams will be slightly happy with where the game is heading too, and the contest actually is hanging in the balance too.
Pitching around leg and spinning away. Dhananjaya keeps his composure this time and pads it away to see the end of the day unbeaten. STUMPS ON DAY 2!

NOT OUT! Dhananjaya has survived a huge scare here. But what was that shot? There was no need whatsoever for this shot when the end of the day is just at the end of this over. It is a nothing delivery! Short and down the leg side, a nothing delivery from Cornwall. Dhananjaya can leave it alone easily. But he goes for the pull. he misses it but the West Indies players go up in a confident appeal. The umpire though stands his ground unmoved. Kraigg Brathwaite thinks about the review but Jermaine Blackwood is convinced. He signals the 'T' straightaway. His skipper goes along with Blackwood and reviews it. Replays roll in and Ultra Edge shows some spike as the ball is closer to the face of the backside of the bat. The umpire keeps rock and rolling and sees some gap when there is a spike. A very good call is made as the giant screen shows NOT OUT.

Review for caught behind! Looks to be close and that too, at the end of the day. Blackwood was certain that this was out. Ultra Edge comes in and there is a slight spike as the ball goes by the bat but not sure where it is coming from. Maybe back of the bat but the ball is not close to the bat when the spike appears and the third umpire has a couple of looks to make sure, but in the end, he decides that there is no bat on this. Will remain not out.

Length ball, but too straight and Lahiru clips it down to fine leg for one.
Back of length, outside off. Lahiru walks across and clips it to mid-wicket.
Full ball on the middle stump line. Chandimal digs it out nicely.
Length ball outside off. Chandimal goes for the drive but gets an inside edge to mid-wicket.
Fuller this time, outside off and Chandimal lets it go.
Lets it go on a length, outside off. Chandimal pushes it to covers.
Good length delivery, on off and Chandimal defends it nicely.
Full one, on middle and Chandimal plays it back to Mayers.
Length delivery, a bit closer to the stumps. But Lahiru won't offer a stroke.
Good length ball but wide outside off. Lahiru allows the keeper to collect it.
Too full, outside off and Lahiru drives this through covers for a couple.
Short of a length, on middle. Lahiru clips it to deep mid-wicket and comes back for the second. Joshua deflects the throw onto the stumps but Lahiru is in.
Fuller delivery on middle and Lahiru plays it to mid-wicket.
Full ball on the pads. Chandimal clips this past mid-wicket for a run.
Length ball, outside off. Chandimal looks to defend but gets the inside edge to fine leg to get off the mark.
Good length delivery but wide outside off, Chandimal lets it go.
Who comes in now? It is Dinesh Chandimal.

OUT! Umpire's call on hitting and West Indies have broken through! Full ball on off, the ball nips in after pitching. Oshada looks to defend it but is hit on the pads. Big appeal by Windies and umpire has given it. Oshada reviews this one right away. The Ultra Edge is flat and Ball Tracker shows umpire's call on hitting. Finally, the umpire's call works for the hosts.
Back of length, on middle. Oshada plays this to mid-wicket.
Review time! This is for LBW and Oshada Fernando makes the 'T' symbol. Ball Tracker confirms Oshada Fernando's worst fears and he has to go back.
Length ball, a touch straighter this time. Clipped to mid-wicket.
Length ball on off and Oshada defends it nicely.
Who will bowl from the other end? Kyle Mayers, it is.
A bit fuller, on his pads. Lahiru clips this towards deep backward square leg for a couple.
Loopy ball outside off and Lahiru is solid in defence.
Darts this on his middle stump and Lahiru defends.
Flighted ball on middle, defended by Lahiru.
A touch shorter this time, on leg stump and Lahiru clips down to fine leg for two.
We are back for the third and final session of the day. The batters for Sri Lanka, Oshada Fernando and Lahiru Thirimanne make their way out now. Rahkeem Cornwall to bowl now.
... Day 2, Evening session ...
Tossed up on off, pushed to mid on.

Sri Lanka will hope that the pair of Thirimanne and Oshada can see out the majority of the final session as well if not the whole of it. Meanwhile, Brathwaite will hope, just like on Day 1, his side can make a strong comeback in the final session of the day. Who will the day belong to? Join us for the Evening session to find out.

West Indies, on the other hand, have been very tidy with their lines and lengths. This looks like a very timid pitch and has had hardly anything for the bowlers. The hosts though have ensured to not give away freebies regularly and have kept things. Alzarri Joseph was the only bowler to get a wicket.

A grinding session of Test match cricket. Sri Lanka lost their skipper, Dimuth Karunaratne very early into the innings as his poor form in the series continued. Lahiru Thirimanne and Oshada Fernando have since weathered the storm and put on a very good fight out in the middle.
Finishes the session with a good length ball, around off. Oshada defends it watchfully. That will be Tea on Day 2.
Length delivery outside off, Oshada is solid in his defence.
Lands it on a length, outside off and the ball nips back in. Oshada looks to go down the ground but gets the inner half to mid on.
Length ball, around off. defended back by Oshada.
Good length delivery, outside off. Oshada pushes it back to Mayers. Plently of words of encouragement by Joshua behind the stumps.
Full ball, outside off, pushed to mid off.
Short and outside off, Lahiru cuts it but the man at point dives and stops it.
Slower through the air, lands on middle and Lahiru clips this to mid-wicket.
Full ball outside off, Lahiru smothers this to silly point.
Flighted ball outside off, defended to covers by Lahiru.
Loopy ball outside off, Lahiru defends it off the front foot.
Tossed up on off, pushed to mid on.
A touch shorter and on his body, Oshada clips it to fine leg for a couple.

NOT OUT! Umpire's call on hitting and Oshada is safe. Length ball outside off, it nips back in after pitching. Oshada doesn't offer a shot and is struck on the pads. West Indies appeal but the umpire is unmoved. They decide to review this one. No need for Ultra Edge as there was no shot offered. Ball Tracker rolls in and yet again, it is umpire's call on hitting.
Review time! Kraigg Brathwaite makes the 'T' symbol, right at the last second, this time, for the LBW appeal. Fernando offered no shot, so impact won't matter. But the wickets are Umpire's call.
Swing and a miss! Short and wide outside off. Oshada goes for the cut but the ball goes under his bat.
Good length ball on off, Oshada defends it.
Short and wide outside off. Oshada runs it past backward point. The fielder chases it but they take two runs.
Serves a length ball, on off. Oshada defends it off the front foot.
Fuller ball on middle and Lahiru pushes it back to Cornwall.
Tossed up delivery on off, Lahiru offers a solid defence.
Flighted ball on middle, clipped to mid-wicket.
Loopy ball on off, defended off the front foot.
A touch shorter on middle. Lahiru defends it off the back foot.
Tossed up on middle, Lahiru defends it back.
Beaten! Good length ball, around off. Ferando looks to force it through the off side but the ball whizzes past his bat. Maiden over.
Bowling in change. Rahkeem Cornwall to roll his arm now.
Full ball, outside off. Pushed to covers.
Length delivery outside off, Fernando waits for it and plays it late to second slip.
A touch fuller this time, outside off and Fernando pushes it to covers.
Serves a length ball, outside off. Fernando prods forward and defends it.
Length ball, right on off stump. Pushed back to mid on by Fernando.
Back of good length, lands on middle and angles across the stumps. Lahiru stands tall and defends it.
Another short one! Short ball on off and Lahiru ducks under it again.
Length ball, pitches on middle and goes down the leg side. Lahiru looks to flciks it but misses.
Effort ball by Holder! Digs this one short and outside off. Lahiru ducks under it.
Good length delivery, around off. Defended by Lahiru.
Good running between the wickets! Length ball on middle and Lahiru flicks it towards deep square leg for a couple.
Good length ball, on middle and off. Defended by Fernando.
Length ball, outside off, defended off the front foot.
A touch fuller this time, on off. Played back to the bowler.
Good length ball, on middle. Defended back to the bowler.
A touch shorter this time, outside off. Fernando stands tall and defends it.
Length ball, outside off. Fernando pushes it to covers.
Kyle Mayers is introduced into the attack.
Good length delivery, a touch outside off. Lahiru defends it watchfully.
A touch fuller, on off. Lahiru defends it off the front foot and takes the bottom hand off the handle at the last moment.
Serves a length ball, around off. Lahiru plays it off the back foot.
Hits the deck on a length, outside off. Lahiru covers his stumps and defends it.
Length ball on middle stump line. Defended off the crease by Lahiru.
Serves a length ball, but wide outside off. Lahiru lets it go.
Back of a length, the ball lands on off and nips back in a bit. But it is still wide enough for Fernando to let it go.
A touch fuller, on middle. Lahiru works this to mid-wicket and picks up a run.
Good length delivery, outside off. Lahiru leaves it alone.
A touch shorter this time, outside off. Lahiru goes across the line and plays it to point.
Length ball on middle, defended.
FOUR! Elegant by Lahiru Thirimanne. Overpitched ball on off and he punches it down the ground and to the long on fence. 50 up for the Sri Lankans.
Good length delivery, on the off stump line. Fernando, who is standing outside his batting crease, defends it back to Holder.
Hits the deck on a length but wide outside off. Oshada lets it go.
Length delivery, around off. Oshada plays it with soft hands to point.
Full delivery on off. Oshada looks to go down the ground but gets the inner half of the bat to mid on.

UPDATE 1412 local (1812 GMT) - Looks like the drizzle has stopped and the covers have also been removed now. Now, the umpires walk out into the middle and the West Indian players follow them out. So, a very short stoppage in play and let's hope that there are no more stoppages now. The Sri Lankan batters, Oshada Fernando and Lahiru Thirimanne come out too. Jason Holder to complete his over.
Good length delivery, just outside off. Oshada waits for it and plays it late to third slip.

UPDATE 1408 local (1808 GMT) - Looks like there is some drizzle and so the umpires have asked for the covers to be brought on. The players are walking off but the rain does not seem to be too heavy. Looks like a passing shower. Let's hope that this shower passes by quickly.
Full ball on off, Oshada defends it back to Holder.
Length ball, just around off. Lahiru covers his stumps and lets it go.
Overpitched ball, outside off. Lahiru leans into it and plays it to mid off.
Full ball on off, defended back to the bowler.
FOUR! Edged and four! Length ball outside off and Lahiru goes for the drive. He gets a thick outside edge and ball goes high and past gully into the ropes.
FOUR! Cracking shot! Full ball outside off and Lahiru creams this through covers and into the ropes.
Full ball on the pads, Lahiru flicks this to deep square leg for a couple.
Good length ball on middle, Oshada defends it well.

NOT OUT! Umpire's call on hitting and Fernando is safe! Back of a length ball on middle and leg. Oshada looks to flick it but misses and gets hit on the pads. West Indies appeal very loudly but the umpire is unmoved. Kraigg Brathwaite shows the 'T' and we go upstairs. Ultra Edge confirms no bat and Ball Tracker confirms that it was umpire's call on hitting the stumps.

Review time! It looked like a close call for LBW and Kraigg Brathwaite wants this one checked upstairs. Ultra Edge shows no bat. Ball Tracker shows that the wickets are Umpire's Call and hence, the review is retained. Oshada Fernando does not lose his wicket though.
Length ball, drifing down the leg stump. Fernando looks to flick it but misses.
Full ball, outside off. Holder wants Fernando to drive but it is left alone.
Back of a length, on off. Lahiru walks across the stumps and clips it to fine leg for one.
Good length delivery, around off. Lahiru defends it from his crease.
Battle of patience out there in the middle! Length ball but on the sixth stump line. Fernando shoulders his arms.
Fuller this time, but again wide outside off. Fernando lets it go.
Good length ball, wide outside off and Fernando won't chase that.
Beaten! Length ball on off, the ball nips back in and goes past Fernando's attempted defence.
Short of a length, outside off. Fernando shuffles across only to leave it in the end.
Length delivery but wide outside off. Left alone.
Comes 'round the wicket and hits the deck on a length, just outside off. Lahiru covers his stumps and blocks it out.
Full ball, but wide outside off. Lahiru won't chase that one.
Good length ball, around off and Lahiru pushes it to mid off.
Full ball, on the fifth stump line. Lahiru lets it go through.
Overpitched ball outside off, Lahiru leans into it and drives this past covers for two runs.
Good length ball, on middle. Lahiru defends it. No ball given as Holder had overstepped.
Starts off with a full ball around off. Lahiru defends it watchfully.
Bowling change. Time for Jason Holder to have a crack, with the ball now.
Serves a length ball, on the sixth stump line. Fernando lets it go.
Length ball, just outside off and defended.

FOUR! Just short of second slip! Length ball outside off, Fernando hangs his bat out there looking to defend it. But gets the thick outside egde, it drops in front of second slip and goes to the ropes.
Short and wide outside off. Punches to covers.
Well bowled! The pressure seems to be getting to him! Length ball, outside off. Fernando shimmies down and shuffles across but leaves it in the end.
Full delivery outside off. Fernando lunges forward and pushes it to point.

DRINKS! A very good hour of play for West Indies. The pace trio have bowled well and kept things very tight with Alzarri Joseph also getting the better of the Sri Lankan skipper. The tourists need to keep their patience and continue to fight calmly. Both Thirimane and Oshada Fernando scored runs in the last innings of the previous Test and the pair will look to put on another big stand.
Good length delivery, on middle and leg. Fernando helps it on its way to fine leg. Single taken.
Fuller ball on middle and off, Fernando shuffles across and plays it to mid on.
Length ball, a touch outside off. Fernando pushes it to covers.
Hits the deck on a good length, on off. Fernando offers the full face of his bat.
Intent from Fernando! Short ball on off and he pulls it past mid-wicket for a couple.
Good length delivery, on the off stump. Fernando gets in line and defends it.
Hits the deck on a length, a touch outside off. Lahiru is aware of his off pole and lets it go.
Back of a length ball, on the fourth stump line. Lahiru defends it watchfully.
A touch fuller this time, on off. Lahiru pushes this to mid on.
Good length ball, on off. Lahiru is solid in his defence.
Overpitched ball outside off. Oshada leans into it and punches it past covers. The fielder chases it but they have enough time to pick up three.
Full ball on off, Lahiru walks across and clips it down to fine leg for a run.
Kemar Roach (2-1-6-0) is back into the attack.
Good length ball, a touch outside off and Fernando shoulders his arms.
Full ball, around off, defended by Fernando.
Short ball, outside off. Fernando gets on top of the bounce and cuts it to point.
Back of a length, outside off. Fernando defends it off the back foot.
A touch fuller this time, on off. Oshada pushes it to extra cover.
Length ball, on off. Fernando watchfully plays it to extra cover.
Too full and on the pads of Lahiru. He nicely clips it towards deep mid-wicket for a couple.
Full ball, wide outside off. Lahiru leans into it and drives it to cover.
Gabriel fires a fast yorker on the stumps and Lahiru keeps it out.
A touch fuller, on the sixth stump line. Lahiru gets in line of the ball and then leaves it alone.
Short of a good length, outside off. Fernando pushes this past covers and takes off for a quick single.
Low full toss on the stumps. Oshada hits it back to Gabriel.
Too full and on his pads, Oshada clips this to deep square leg for one.
Good length ball, just around off. Oshada stands tall and defends it.
A touch fuller on his pads, Oshada clips this past mid-wicket for a couple and gets off the mark.
Length ball on middle, defended.
Hits the deck on a length, outside off. Oshada looks to defend but is hit on the pads. West Indies appeal loudly but the umpire is unmoved. Replay shows that the impact was outside off.

OUT! TAKEN! Brilliant take by Bonner at the third slip! This is another disappointment from Dimuth and he will be kicking himself as he goes back for the very low score of just 1. Length ball, outside off, and Dimuth is drawn into a drive. His feet go nowhere and he gets an outside edge. The ball is flying to the right of Nkrumah Bonner but he puts in a good dive and completes a stunner to remove the Sri Lankan skipper.
Who will come out at Number 3? Oshada Fernando, it is.
Length ball, on the fourth stump line. Lahiru covers his stumps and then shoulders his arms.
Good length ball, outside off. Lahiru comes forward and punches it to mid on.
Short of good length, outside off. Lahiru pushes this to covers and looks for a single. He is sent back by Dimuth.
Short stuff again! This time a touch outside off. Lahiru again ducks under it.
Effort ball by Gabriel! Digs this in short, on off. Lahiru ducks under it.
Well bowled! Length ball, right in the corridor of uncertainty. Lahiru leaves it alone.
A touch fuller, but wide outside off. Dimuth puts in a stride and then shoulders his arms.
Digs this a touch shorter, on middle and Dimuth defends it well.
Good length ball, on the fifth stump line. Left alone by Dimuth.
A touch shorter this time, outside off. Lahiru gets on top of the bounce and places it behind point for one.
Good length ball, wide outside off. Left alone.
Length ball outside off, Lahiru waits for it and then guides it past point for a couple.
Another full delivery on the middle pole, Lahiru Thirimanne tucks this one to the right of the square leg fielder, for a single. 7 off this over!
Another length ball outside off, Lahiru Thirimanne makes another leave.

FOUR! Too full and Lahiru Thirimanne does not hesitate in sending the ball to the ropes. Too full and around off, Lahiru Thirimanne comes ahead and punches this one through the mid off region and the ball dribbles through to the ropes. Second boundary for Lahiru!
Fuller again, but this time it is on leg, Lahiru Thirimanne flicks this one through square leg for a brace now.
Fuller and outside off, Lahiru Thirimanne gets a full stride forward and drives this one to the short cover fielder, who does well to move to his left and stop the ball.
On a good length and around off, Lahiru Thirimanne leaves the ball, as the ball, with the angle, just zips past the off pole.
Another full length delivery, this time way outside the off pole, DK watches it sail into the keeper's mitts.
This is on a length and outside off, Lahiru Thirimanne drives this one nicely through covers. Gets a single by the time, the fielder can chase and stop the ball.
Another full ball which is at a yorker length, on the off pole. Lahiru does well to get his bat across and keep this one out.
A length ball, outside the off pole, Lahiru Thirimanne has no problems in leaving this one alone.
Fuller, almost yorker length outside off, Lahiru Thirimanne digs this one out.
Outside off, left alone.
Change. Alzarri Joseph has been introduced into the attack.
On a good length and around off, pushed back to the bowler. A slow and steady start for the Lankans.
Fuller and on off, Dimuth Karunaratne pushes this one to the mid on fielder.
Short and outside off this time, Dimuth Karunaratne looks to slam this one through the covers but his shot comes off the lower half of the willow and goes to the fielder at covers instead.
Full on off, played towards mid off.

Well bowled this time. A back of a length ball around off, Dimuth Karunaratne looks to have a feel of the ball but the ball nips back in sharply and goes past the inside edge, into the keeper's mitts.
Fuller and around off, punched through mid off for a single, as the fielder runs behind and stops the ball.
Maiden! Outside off, no shot offered to this delivery.
Now, makes him play at this as this is closer to the off pole and on length, Dimuth Karunaratne tucks this one to the square leg fielder.
Kemar Roach sticks with his line and length again. Dimuth Karunaratne sticks to his plan of letting the ball go.
The third ball of the over is an action replay of the first 2 balls.
Similar line and length, just like the last ball, Dimuth makes another leave here.
Fuller and wide outside off now, Dimuth Karunaratne makes a well calculated leave.

On a length and outside off, the ball shoots up after hitting the deck as Lahiru lets this one through and Rahkeem Cornwall at first slip, does well to stop the ball as the ball swung into his direction.
Back of a length and on middle, LT shuffles across and works this one to the square leg fielder again.
Angling into the batter and around off, Lahiru Thirimanne gets low and looks to drive but the ball takes the inner half of the bat and goes through square leg.
Fuller length ball on the pads, Lahiru Thirimanne looks to flick this one but he misses and the ball takes the pad and goes to the leg slip fielder, on the bounce.
A length ball on off, LT is solid in his defense.
Shannon Gabriel starts off with a length delivery, outside off but angling into the left-hander. Lahiru Thirimanne just shoulders arms this time.
Single to end the over. 6 off the first over. Length ball on off, Thirimanne places it to cover and keeps the strike with a single.
Good length ball on off, Thirimanne defends it.
Good length delivery outside off. Roach pulls his length back and this is much better. Thirimanne shoulders arms to it.

FOUR! Beautiful shot to get off the mark! Roach goes full on off, Thirimanne gets on his front foot and just times his drive through mid off for a boundary.  This shot will give him a lot of confidence. Excellent way to get your innings underway.
Who will bowl from the other end? It is Shannon Gabriel.
Slightly fuller on off, Thirimanne begins his innings with a solid defense.

Sri Lanka and Dimuth Karunaratne are up and running straightaway! Roach starts with a good length delivery on off with a little shape on it. Karunaratne taps it towards cover and takes a quick single to get off the mark.
